fatal_errors: Fails to identify the specific AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA and its as-cast FCC+B2 microstructure.
Substitutes broad service/testing temperatures for the required intermediate-temperature aging treatment.
Incorrectly attributes the transition to suppression of temper embrittlement rather than reproducing an aging-induced brittle window.
Omits the enhanced L12 ordering, jagged B2/FCC phase boundaries, elevated APBE, planar slip, and phase-boundary stress concentration that cause embrittlement.
Does not identify the approximately 600°C ductility minimum or recovery near 750°C.
Provides no cited evidence and proposes only generic mechanical testing that cannot distinguish the target mechanism.
explanation: The response recognizes that a high-entropy-alloy system is relevant and gives an appropriate conventional-alloy baseline, but it does not reconstruct the reported material, treatment, temperature window, or mechanism. Its example CoCrFeMnNi and -196°C to 1000°C testing range are not supported by the target. Moreover, claiming that inherent suppression of temper embrittlement enables the transition is conceptually inconsistent with the target result, in which AlCoCrFeNi2.1 develops a pronounced aging-induced ductility minimum at 600°C through L12 ordering and jagged B2/FCC boundaries, followed by recovery at 750°C. The proposed experiment could establish a generic non-monotonic ductility trend but could not test the decisive microstructural mechanism.
